newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Jet well bid, diesel well offered.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Jet well bid, diesel well offered.

text.p: Singapore physical jet fuel price maintained its uptrend on Thursday as more buyers emerged while sellers were scarce, but gas oil saw more sellers, traders said.
Jet fuel buyers bid as high as $30.75-$30.80 for second-half February lifting cargoes free-on-board (fob) basis, traders said. These were higher than the deal on Wednesday at $30.40 a barrel.
Late in the day a European major sold 150,000 barrels of jet fuel to a Singapore trader at $30.75 for Feb 15-19 lifting fob.
The scarcity of offers lent credence to earlier talks that February jet fuel barrels have almost dried up.
Unlike gas oil, jet fuel prices have been relatively steady, dipping to a low of $26.75 in August to a high of $35.15 in December.
Gas oil bottomed at $24.45 in August, peaked at $34.65 in December before falling to around $25.00 in January. Physical gas oil prices are currently volatile, being offered between $25.30 and $26.50.
Traders said while a local trader was keen to see prices slip below $25.00 with its aggressive offers, a major was intent to see prices supported above $26.00 a barrel.
Amid an absence in regional demand, buyers are content at seeing the offers pass for the moment until a clearer price direction emerges, traders said.
The strength in physical jet prices was also helping to widen the swaps jet/gas oil spread to $3.80/$4.00 a barrel on Thursday from Wednesday's $3.30 bid.

In the only tender news of the day, French oil firm Total was set to win Sri Lanka's import tender for gas oil and jet fuel with its offer at 58 cents per barrel above Singapore spot quotes c&f basis. The combination cargo is for February 13-14 lifting.
